cascade.projectName: Connecting Power: Scaling and Sharing Sub-Granting Experiences to Prevent and Combat Gender-Based Violence Across Europe
cascade.furtherInfo:
The CoPower project is implemented by Oxfam Italia ETS, Action Aid Hellas, Asociación Bienestar y Desarolloa and We World-GVC. It started on 1 March 2026 and will end on 28 February 2029.
 Its objective is to strengthen the capacity of Civil Society Organisation (CSOs) to provide safe and inclusive services for victims of gender-based violence (GBV) against women, girls, and children in all their diversity across six European countries: Italy, Greece, Spain, Serbia, Romania, and Albania.
 The project foresees three national calls, along with transnational calls involving the following country pairs: Italy–Serbia, Spain-Romania, and Greece-Albania. The national calls will fund at least 10 projects in Italy, 10 in Spain and 10 in Greece. The transnational calls will fund 5 projects for Italy and Serbia, 5 projects for Spain and Romania and 5 projects for Greece and Albania. Overall, a minimum of 60 CSOs will be engaged, fostering meaningful cross-country cooperation.
 A comprehensive capacity-sharing programme for CSOs will include needs assessments, training, mentoring, and both national and international workshops to promote mutual learning and support in the full implementation of the EU Violence Against Women Directive.
cascade.howTo:
The CoPower Action has been designed to directly fund initiatives addressing Gender Based Violence(GBV) against women, girls and children through an intersectional approach .
 All eligible activities supported through the project calls will directly respond to the multidimensional and intersecting needs of women, girls, and child survivors of GBV, strengthening an inclusive and accessible protection systems across different intervention contexts. Child protection and gender mainstreaming are expected to be integral components of the proposals submitted by CSOs, while partner organisations will provide dedicated technical support to improve the capacities of participating CSOs in these areas.

The primary target group, will include Women’s rights organisations (WROs), Anti-violence centres and anti-trafficking centres, Human rights, LGBTIQ+ rights, child rights, social inclusion and disability, elderly, migrant and refugee organisations.

cascade.howTo:
1. Purpose of the call 
 The UPC is opening a call for grants to support students of the Master's Degree in Electronic Engineering (hereinafter, MEE Master's Degree) taught at the UPC's Barcelona School of Telecommunications Engineering (ETSETB).
 The aim of these scholarships is to provide financial assistance to MEE students interested in academic training activities in the field of electronics that involve mobility to any of the foreign institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project. The grants cover expenses related to double degree programs and short-term mobility stays at these institutions.
 2. Characteristics of the grants 
 All eligible expenses in this call and described in this document are linked to activities that involve international mobility to one of the foreign institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project.
 This call offers 6 different types of grants. The same student can apply for grants corresponding to different blocks, but the maximum amount they can receive in this call will be €10,000, regardless of the limits established in each of the blocks.

records.description:
About Phortify 
 Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.
 About the Phortify Funding Framework 
 Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

 BiodivFuture focuses on supporting future-looking research and innovation that will address biodiversity and novel ecosystems, as well as their socio-ecological dynamics and consequences relating to the sustainability goals of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and associated future pathways and trajectories of change. The call covers investigating the causes (drivers), effects (biological responses), and outcomes (including opportunities, risks and trade-offs) of current and future trajectories of change in all relevant realms (terrestrial, freshwater, marine and coastal areas), in all regions of the world . It aims at funding novel, high-quality transnational research with potential for societal and political impact that will significantly improve our understanding of novel ecosystems with holistic, systemic, and integrated approaches.
 In the face of inevitable and potentially irreversible change, knowledge generated under this call should ultimately lead to actions to achieve impacts that sustain resilient, interconnected, diverse and ecologically functioning ecosystems. This could include critical reflection on what constitutes ecosystem states that best preserve or restore natural resources by taking multiple costs and benefits (trade-offs) into account and the diversity of contexts, scales, perspectives and world views. records.description:
The FOREST Joint Call 2026 – ForestPathways supports transnational research and innovation activities across the spectrum from fundamental research to applied research and, where appropriate, demonstration activities. Projects are expected to generate new knowledge, develop practical solutions, and contribute to implementation in policy, management or industry contexts, while considering the diversity of forests and the forest-based sector.
 Applicants must select the single topic that best reflects the primary focus of their proposal. Proposals may address multiple topics but will be evaluated and ranked under one primary topic.
 TOPIC 1 – Climate-Resilient Forest Systems: “How forests function and respond to climate change” 
 This topic supports research and innovation addressing the resilience, adaptive capacity, and long-term sustainability of forest ecosystems under changing environmental conditions, including climate change and increasing disturbance pressures. It aims to strengthen the scientific basis for climate-resilient forest systems and support their adaptation and mitigation to climate change, within broader environmental and socioeconomic contexts.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, carbon dynamics measurement, monitoring and assessment of carbon stocks and sinks; adaptation pathways and strategies; forest ecosystem processes and dynamics; disturbance regimes, including wildfires and other abiotic and biotic disturbances, pests and diseases; landscape-level interactions and spatial dynamics; and genetic diversity and adaptive capacity, including assisted migration.
 TOPIC 2 – Adaptive and Multifunctional Forest Management Systems: “How forests should be managed under changing conditions” 
 This topic supports research and innovation focused on the implementation of adaptive and multifunctional forest management systems that enhance resilience, sustainability, and the provision of multiple ecosystem services. It aims to support forest management approaches capable of responding to ecological change, disturbance risks, and evolving environmental, economic, and societal demands.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, silvicultural systems and management approaches supporting resilient and multifunctional forests; sustainable harvesting and wood mobilisation methods; monitoring, assessment and planning tools for adaptive management; integration of forest genetic resources into management strategies; operational, digital and technical innovations; risk reduction and adaptation strategies; and trade-offs and synergies between ecosystem services.
 TOPIC 3 – Timber and Innovative Wood-Based Products: “How wood is transformed into innovative products” 
 This topic supports research and innovation on the development, performance, and uptake of timber and innovative wood-based products contributing to decarbonisation and the circular bioeconomy. It aims to advance the development and market uptake of sustainable wood-based products and systems, supporting the substitution of fossil-based and carbon-intensive materials and contributing to low-carbon construction and manufacturing.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, engineered timber and timber construction systems; high-value wood-based products, chemicals and materials; substitution of fossil-based and other carbon-intensive materials; more sustainable alternatives to polluting wood treatments and processing practices; standardisation, testing and certification; circular and resource-efficient use of wood-based products; innovative use of underutilised softwood and hardwood species; innovative manufacturing technologies; and approaches to increase market demand and consumer acceptance and uptake.

cascade.org: Multi-national Investigator-Initiated Clinical Studies in Cardiovascular, Autoimmune, Metabolic, and Non-Communicable Respiratory Diseases, including Underrepresented Populations (IICS4all 2027)
cascade.projectName: Fostering a European Research Area for Health Research
cascade.furtherInfo:
The aim of the call is to support pragmatic, phase III, randomised controlled, multi-national interventional Investigator-Initiated Clinical Studies (IICS) 
 (1) that are designed as following study types :
 - comparative-effectiveness studies and/or
- drug repurposing studies of off-patent drugs
 Applicants can make use of existing cohorts, e.g. for designing Trials within Cohorts (TwiCs).
 (2) that have a high public relevance in the fields of these specific diseases or conditions (that are of equal importance):
 - Cardiovascular diseases
- Metabolic disorders
- Autoimmune diseases
- Non-communicable respiratory diseases
 The multi-national Investigator-Initiated Clinical Studies should primarily address at least one of the abovementioned principal diseases/conditions, although the proposals can also address several of the mentioned diseases/conditions and/or in combination with related comorbidities.
 (3) that ensure inclusivity and diversity in the study population and also include sex/gender-sensitive, age-specific or other diversity-related aspects , if reasonable.
 Out of Scope 
 · Clinical studies conducted for direct commercial purposes
 · For drug repurposing studies: a drug still on patent in one of the participating countries. This criterion also applies to biological medicinal products and biosimilars.
 · Phase I and Phase II studies: Studies in which a treatment is used in humans for the first time, or which are aimed exclusively at assessing tolerability, safety or dose determination
 · Proposals focused on observational studies, non-interventional cohort studies, implementation studies, translational/clinical approval studies, creation of large databases, systematic reviews and meta-analysis. Non-randomised studies.
 · Studies in other medical areas which are not mentioned above (cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, autoimmune diseases and non-communicable respiratory diseases). Particularly, those clinical studies that are focused on cancer

records.description:
Project proposals should address multidisciplinary research. 
 The aim of this call is to support translational research projects that develop application(s) of nanotechnologies, either solely or in combination with Key Enabling Technologies (KETs), to make significant strides in the development of diagnostic and theranostic tools for Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs). Proposals should focus on developing and/or validating diagnostic and theranostic tools that are grounded in robust scientific evidence. The results obtained from these tools must enable the optimisation of the care continuum. This care continuum includes, among other things, prevention, early disease detection, disease monitoring, treatment guidance, adverse effect and/or risk/benefit assessment.
 The proposed research must define and validate performance benchmarks against existing diagnostic approaches to demonstrate added value in terms of sensitivity, specificity, accessibility, affordability, patient comfort, invasiveness and/or safety.
 In addition, at any stage of the research and for all applications, translational and adoption requirements for nano-enabled diagnostic and theranostic solutions must be considered. This includes scalability, manufacturability, standardisation, affordability, accessibility, cost-effectiveness, regulatory readiness, interoperability, and integration across different healthcare systems.
 In case of the development of theranostic tool(s), the proposed approach must apply a diagnostic-first principle, where diagnostic must serve the therapeutic choice.
 Additional points should be considered beyond the research topics. Please for more detail, consult the call text on ERA4Health website .

SME Market Expansion Open Call 2027
 Opportunity
 09/10/2026 10.00 - CET 
 01/12/2026 17.00 - CET 
 Mobility
 The EIT Urban Mobility is thrilled to launch the new edition of the SME Market Expansion Open Call. 
 The Call is designed to promote business growth and market expansion, encouraging the replication and scaling of successful solutions in new regions or sectors. It offers a strategic platform for SMEs with ambitions to scale by expanding into new markets.
 The Call focus is on accelerating the market uptake of impactful innovations by reducing the risk of development and deployment. EIT Urban Mobility aims to support solutions with a clear path to market, helping cities and businesses confidently procure and scale proven innovations. Through collaboration with an end-client, SMEs can validate their offering in a real-world setting, while gaining visibility and credibility in the European market.
 The Call will focus on five topics:
 - Public and Shared Transport
- Urban Logistics
- Electrification of transport and alternative fuels
- Mobility data management
- Health and mobility
 EIT funding allocation
 The total estimated funding allocated to this Call is €600 000. Around 10 projects are to be implemented by 10 different SMEs. Each awarded entity will receive a fixed lump sum grant of EUR 60 000.
 Who can apply?
 This Call is a mono-beneficiary call addressed to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that are supported by an end client, a public or private entity, committed to testing and demonstrating the solution.
 To ensure a balanced portfolio of projects, SMEs selected for the previous SME Market Expansion Open Call 2026 are not eligible to apply for this Call.
 Info session
 Info webinar and contact details are available to guarantee the maximum support to the applicants during the proposal’s preparation process.
 To help applicants with the preparation and submission of their proposals, EIT Urban Mobility will host one live Call info webinar focused on the Call content, calendar, scope, topics, KPIs, the submission and evaluation tools and procedures, end-client role, and the financial aspects including contribution to EIT Urban Mobility financial sustainability.
 Info webinar: 15 October 2026 10.00 – 11.00 CET. Register and watch on Zoom .

 Opportunity
 14/10/2026 11.00 - CET 
 13/01/2027 16.00 - CET 
 EIT
 EIT Health’s Innovation Validation Call 2027 supports innovative digital and AI-powered medical technologies that are ready for real-world clinical validation and are approaching market launch. 
 This call addresses the funding gap for solutions that need to run clinical studies and collect evidence to demonstrate safety and efficacy, apply for regulatory approval and prepare for commercialisation. 
 Who can apply? 
 Consortia must comprise at least two organisations from different countries, representing at least two sides of the Knowledge Triangle (industry, research, education). A commercialising company must lead the project. Eligible solutions must be digital or AI-enabled medical devices (MDR/IVDR) at Innovation Maturity Level 6 (IML 6), aiming to reach IML 7 by project end. Please refer to EIT Health’s Healthcare Innovation Cycle Framework for more information on the required Innovation Maturity Level for this call. 
 Funding 
 EIT Health will fund up to 50% of the total project budget, up to €850,000 per project. 
 The commercialising entity must sign a Financial Sustainability Contribution Agreement and, if it is a micro or small enterprise, must receive €400,000–€500,000 of the grant. 
 What we fund 
 Funding supports activities enabling clinical validation (i.e. pivotal clinical studies), regulatory submission (i.e. CE-mark application dossier), product finalisation, market readiness and commercial strategy. 
 Expected outcomes 
 Solutions must have the potential to impact 150,000 patients or citizens in the EU and aim to be on the market and generating at least €10,000 in revenues within three years after the funding period. 
 Key dates 
 - Call opens on: 14 October 2026 
- Call closes on: 13 January 2027 
- Call information session: 28 October at 12.00 CET – Register here 
- Open Q&A session: 1 December at 15.00 CET – Register here 
 Where to find out more

 How to apply 
 - Step 1: Register your organisation in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal to obtain the nine-digit Participant Identification Code (PIC). If you do not know if your organisation already has a PIC number, you can check whether your organisation is already registered on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal . 
- Step 2: Apply to the call via EIT Health’s application platform. Click the ‘Apply’ button below.

EIT Higher Education Initiative Call for Proposals 2026
 Opportunity
 20/10/2026 11.00 - CET 
 13/01/2027 17.00 - CET 
 EIT
 The EIT Higher Education Initiative Call is now open!
 The call is offering up to €1.25 million per project over 18 months, with a total budget of €40 million, to strengthen innovation and entrepreneurship capacity in higher education, focusing on manufacturing and deep tech. It will support projects that help universities develop innovation and entrepreneurship skills, improve technology transfer services and build stronger links with businesses. 
 Projects will focus on three key areas: 
 - STEM talent for innovation and entrepreneurship: Developing innovation, entrepreneurship and intellectual property skills among students and staff in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) and related fields. 
- Institutional capacity for knowledge valorisation and innovation: Strengthening universities' ability to turn research and knowledge into innovations, including through improved technology transfer, intellectual property management and support for startups. 
- Integration into innovation ecosystems: Building stronger links between higher education institutions, businesses, research organisations, investors and innovation networks, particularly in manufacturing and deep tech. 
 Eligibility and consortium requirements 
 Who can apply?
 To be eligible, consortia must meet the following requirements:
 - Consortium composition: Each consortium must include at least five funded partners: at least three HEIs (from three different Horizon Europe-eligible countries, including at least one EU Member State) and at least two business/industry partners and/or business/industry representative organisations (e.g. SMEs, startups, larger enterprises and industry associations). Industry partners operating in manufacturing or deep-tech technologies are strongly encouraged to join a consortium. 
- Eligibility: Organisations funded under the EIT HEI Call 2025 are not eligible to apply under the 2026 call. Each organisation may participate as a funded beneficiary in only one 2026 call application. 
 How to apply 
 Consortia of higher education institutions, businesses, research organisations, public bodies and other non-academic partners can prepare their applications by consulting the full  call text   and finding potential partners through the  matchmaking platform . 
 Selected projects will be announced later in 2027.

Catalyse NEB 2027 Open Call
 Opportunity
 29/10/2026 14.00 - CET 
 15/01/2027 17.00 - CET 
 Grow your startup with the New European Bauhaus
 Catalyse NEB is the EIT Community New European Bauhaus (NEB) accelerator for startups integrating sustainability, aesthetics and inclusion into their businesses, products and services.
 The New European Bauhaus is an EU initiative that aims to make places and ways of living more sustainable, inclusive and beautiful.
 The programme will support 20 startups that address community needs in areas related to climate, food or urban mobility.
 How it works   
 Each selected startup receives a €22 000 grant and tailored business support, including:    
 - tailored one-to-one business and design mentoring;   
 - workshops covering business development, communications and New European Bauhaus values;   
 - online and in-person networking activities; 
 - visibility opportunities throughout the programme.   
 Who can apply?   
 Both EIT KIC partners and non-partners may apply. Applicants must:   
 - be a for-profit startup incorporated after 1 January 2022 in an eligible country: an EU Member State, a linked Overseas Country or Territory, or a third country associated to Horizon Europe Pillar 3; 
 - have a registered Participant Identification Code at the time of application;

Proof of Concept & Technology Validation Call
 Opportunity
 06/11/2026 12.00 - CET 
 18/01/2027 12.00 - CET 
 Food
 The EIT Food Biotech Proof of Concept Call helps biotech startups bridge two critical gaps in technology development: Route 1 (Validation) for technologies at TRL 4–6 and Route 2 (Demonstrator) for technologies at TRL 7–9. 
 A ‘Proof of Concept’ is a small-scale project that tests whether a technology, product or service can work in practice and meet the needs of a potential customer. For biotech startups, this stage is critical because many promising innovations fail before they reach the market due to two distinct funding and development gaps, often referred to as ‘valleys of death’. 
 To address these challenges, the EIT Food Biotech Proof of Concept Call offers two funding routes, each targeting a different valley of death and stage of technology development. 
 Route 1 (Validation) addresses the first valley of death, which typically occurs at lower technology readiness levels (TRLs), when a startup has promising science but lacks the validation, infrastructure and industry partnerships needed to reduce the risks of applying the technology in real-world settings. 
 Technologies at TRL 4, 5 or 6 must be submitted under Route 1 (see the Route 1 Guidelines). 
 Apply to Route 1 
 Route 2 (Demonstrator) addresses the second valley of death, which occurs later, when a startup has a validated, lower-risk technology but needs larger-scale demonstration, co-financing and industrial partnerships to move towards commercial deployment and market uptake. Technologies that have reached TRL 7 (system prototype demonstrated in an operational environment) or higher should be submitted under Route 2. Technologies already at TRL 9 (actual system proven in an operational environment) are eligible if the project takes the solution to commercial volumes or validates it in a new application or market. 
 Apply to Route 2 
 The routes do not overlap: the TRL reached by the call deadline determines the appropriate route, and the same technology cannot be submitted under both routes. 
 Together, the two routes provide a pathway for biotech startups to access support at the stage most relevant to their development. Through this call, EIT Food aims to foster collaboration between startups and corporate partners to validate technologies, test commercial assumptions and generate evidence for future growth and investment. This includes, where relevant, facilitating access to pilot facilities, laboratories and other specialised infrastructure available through Alliance members – resources that startups often cannot access or afford on their own. 
 Projects should generate practical evidence, reduce technical and commercial risks, and establish a clear pathway towards further development, expanded pilot testing and market adoption.

 Opportunity
 25/11/2026 17.00 - CET 
 27/01/2027 17.00 - CET 
 Creativity
 EIT Culture & Creativity has announced €1.275 million in funding for Resilience Roadmaps to support ten projects that will translate Europe’s environmental and societal transitions into lasting local change. 
 The ten projects will bring cultural organisations, communities and public authorities together to tackle challenges affecting people and places across Europe. Over 18 months, each project will work with at least 65 community participants, applying cultural, artistic and design practices to co-create a Resilience Roadmap: a living plan that turns locally defined solutions into a clear course for future action, facilitating uptake by public authorities and providing a pathway for wider application. 
 From ten roadmaps to a European body of practice 
 The projects will work across three dimensions of resilience: 
 - Intergenerational fairness: focusing on dialogue and shared decision-making across generations 
- Climate justice: focusing on fair responses to environmental change 
- Community cohesion: focusing on strengthening trust, inclusion and collective responses to shared challenges 
 Acting as future-making laboratories, the ten projects will apply cultural practices, creative approaches and design to prototype solutions across different social, geographical and institutional contexts, showing what can be adapted elsewhere, what depends on local conditions and what enables successful approaches to endure. 
 Taken together, the resulting roadmaps will form a European body of practice, creating transferable knowledge and approaches for cities, regions, cultural organisations and policymakers facing similar challenges. Crucially, they will provide evidence of how place-based approaches can move from local experimentation into sustained public practice. 
 How to apply 
 The Resilience Roadmaps call will provide up to €127 500 per project over 18 months. Projects must be led by a cultural or creative organisation and include at least one public authority. 
 A dedicated information session for applicants will be held on 15 December from 15:30 to 17:00 CET.

records.description: The Opportunity   Tourism is one of Europe's most important economic sectors, contributing significantly to employment, regional development and economic growth. Following the recovery of international travel since COVID-19, destinations across Europe are experiencing increasing visitor numbers while facing growing pressure to manage tourism sustainably, enhance visitor experiences and protect natural and cultural assets.  Destinations, tourism operators and public authorities are looking for innovative digital solutions that support more efficient tourism management, improve visitor services and help balance economic growth with environmental and social sustainability. Challenges such as overtourism, seasonal demand fluctuations, congestion, accessibility, environmental impact and changing traveller expectations require new approaches supported by reliable data and real-time insights.  At the same time, visitors increasingly expect personalised, seamless and digital experiences before, during and after their trips. Meanwhile, tourism stakeholders require better tools to understand visitor flows, monitor destinations, optimise infrastructure, improve safety and support informed decision-making.  Topics of relevance  Visitor flow monitoring and management  Services that monitor and forecast visitor movements, identify congestion and help distribute visitors more effectively. Solutions could include dynamic routing, congestion alerts and decision-support tools for destination managers.   Sustainable tourism and environmental monitoring  Solutions that help destinations and tourism operators assess and reduce their environmental impact. Applications could include monitoring environmental pressures, land-use or coastal changes and emissions, as well as supporting sustainability reporting, responsible destination planning and regenerative tourism models.   Smart cultural and natural heritage management  Services supporting the monitoring and protection of cultural and natural heritage sites. Applications could include site-condition assessment, risk detection, visitor-impact analysis and digital models supporting conservation and long-term asset management.   Seamless mobility and travel experience  Integrated services that make it easier for visitors to combine different transport modes, particularly when accessing rural, remote or less-connected destinations. Applications could include multimodal travel planning, accessibility routing and improved first- and last-mile connectivity.   Immersive and inclusive tourism experiences  Location-based digital services that improve access to cultural and natural assets. These could include augmented and virtual reality experiences, accessible navigation for people with disabilities, digital interpretation tools and remote tourism experiences.   Safety, resilience and crisis support  Services helping travellers, tourism operators and destinations respond to natural hazards, environmental events and operational disruptions. Applications could include situational awareness, location-based alerts, emergency communications and crisis decision-support tools.   Remote connectivity for rural and remote destinations  Connectivity solutions enabling tourism services in areas with limited terrestrial coverage. Applications could support rural tourism businesses, online bookings, digital guest services, Internet of Things monitoring and access to real-time travel and safety information.  Value of Space  Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS)  GNSS can provide precise positioning for visitor flow analysis, navigation, mobility services and accessible routing. It can support the monitoring of visitor movements, helping tourism destinations understand how visitors move between locations, and manage visitor flows more effectively. GNSS can also enable location-based tourism experiences, including digital services that provide information or content according to the visitor’s location. Geofencing, tracking and safety functions can further support visitor management and improve mobility across tourism destinations.   Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO)  SatEO can provide data for environmental monitoring, land-use and coastal-change detection, and the assessment of natural and cultural assets. It can support destinations and tourism operators in monitoring environmental pressures associated with tourism activities and understanding changes affecting sensitive locations. SatEO can also contribute to sustainability indicators, environmental impact assessments and evidence-based destination planning. records.description: A new call focusing on Wildfire Preparedness opened on 1 September 2026. The earlier Wildfire Response call closed on 2 June 2026. Introduction This is part of the Wildfire Safety initiative, inviting proposals for innovative services that advance wildfire management using space technology and data. The first call focused on Wildfire Response, supporting solutions for early detection of wildfires, near-real-time fire evolution monitoring, and fire behaviour simulation and prediction. A subsequent call focusing on Wildfire Preparedness will open on 1 September 2026, and will address wildfire risk assessment, fuel load management, and the application of preventative and adaptation measures. Challenges Wildfires have forever played an integral role in regulating our natural environment; shaping landscapes and sustaining ecosystems. However, in recent years, the frequency and intensity of wildfires in Europe’s Southern Mediterranean region, as well as parts of Central and Eastern Europe, have notably increased. Data from the European Forest Fires Information System (EFFIS) suggests that the average area affected by fires in 2025 in European Union member states was more than double the average from across 2006-2024. Human activity and environmental conditions favouring wildfire ignition and propagation have historically been the catalysts behind such fires. The extension of urban-forest interfaces, where human settlements and flammable vegetation meet, is exacerbating both the risk of fire onset and the magnitude of their impact. The consequences of such are environmental, economic and social. Wildfires cause extensive loss of, and damage to, lives, natural resources, and property. Local economies suffer due to impacts on tourism, abandonment of rural areas and disruption of trade. The burning of biomass releases pollutants negatively impacting air quality and sowing longer-term impacts on human health and the environment. In parallel, on-going advances in space and terrestrial technologies offer novel means to tackle such challenges. Value of space Satellite data and technology must play a critical role in the solutions proposed for this opportunity. Satellite Earth observation for mapping and monitoring of active fires, burn scars, vegetative health, risk factors, vulnerable infrastructure, and otherwise. Satellite positioning to guide aerial platforms (drones and aircraft) for fire monitoring and suppression, geo-referencing of data collected from aerial platforms and in-situ sensors. Satellite communications to provide connectivity to distributed in-situ sensors across a region, as well as communication links for aerial platforms. records.description: The opportunity  This is one of three sub-calls under the Arctic Region Call for Proposals, supporting European space-enabled solutions to address the region's growing operational, environmental and security challenges. Climate change, increasing maritime activity and the growing strategic importance of the Arctic are creating new security and resilience requirements. Critical infrastructure - including ports, energy assets, communication networks and transport corridors - is increasingly exposed to environmental hazards, operational disruptions and malicious activities. Arctic stakeholders require improved capabilities to monitor, protect and respond to emerging threats while maintaining safe and resilient operations across vast and remote territories. This sub-call focuses on security, resilience and critical infrastructure protection. Applications are invited for space-enabled solutions that enhance the monitoring, protection and resilience of critical assets, and support authorities and operators in maintaining security and operational continuity across the Arctic region. Topics of relevance The priority areas below were defined in consultation with Arctic Region stakeholders. Applications are particularly encouraged relating to: critical infrastructure monitoring and protection maritime security and maritime domain awareness detection of anomalous, suspicious or unlawful activities resilience of communication and transport networks emergency preparedness and crisis response cross-border situational awareness and information sharing protection of remote energy, communication and logistics assets Value of Space Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO) can provide persistent monitoring of critical infrastructure, maritime activity and remote operational areas. It can support the detection of unusual patterns of activity, the identification of environmental and operational risks, and the monitoring of changes affecting the integrity of infrastructures such as ports, pipelines, communication facilities and transport networks. InSAR techniques can support the monitoring of ground deformation and infrastructure stability, including risks linked to permafrost degradation. Satellite Communications (Satcom) can provide secure and resilient connectivity across remote Arctic regions where terrestrial networks are unavailable or vulnerable. They can support emergency communications, crisis management, command and control functions, and maintain operational continuity during disruptions affecting critical infrastructure and transportation systems. Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) can enable trusted positioning, navigation and timing services for maritime, air and land operations. They can support asset tracking, geofencing, infrastructure monitoring, incident response coordination and the protection of critical transportation and logistics operations across the Arctic. records.description: The Opportunity   As energy systems face growing operational, environmental and security challenges, ensuring the resilience of Europe's electricity grids is becoming increasingly important. This is driving demand for innovative solutions that can help grid operators anticipate, detect and respond to disruptions, while maintaining a secure and reliable energy supply.  This Call for Proposals is conducted in collaboration with ENTSO-E, the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity. As part of ESA’s Task Force for Innovation in Energy Through Space, ENTSO-E has consolidated a representative set of generic operational challenges for electricity transmission networks, focusing on system operation, resilience, situational awareness and operational efficiency. The Call invites proposals for Proof-of-concept Studies and Pilot Projects for services addressing selected challenges relevant to the resilience and operational continuity of European electricity transmission systems. These include:  growing physical, cyber, and climate-related risks​ to energy infrastructure  increasingly extreme weather events (such as wildfires, floods, storms, heatwaves) affecting grid operations​   increasing dependency on secure infrastructure​ for digitalisation and interconnected power systems, and  economic, societal, and national security impacts from disruption to energy systems  The challenges have been identified through engagement with ENTSO-E and European Transmission System Operators. They are illustrative, intentionally generalised and intended to stimulate innovation. They should not be interpreted as descriptions of the current operational practices, existing capability gaps or specific priorities of ENTSO-E or any individual TSO. Subject to their individual interest and applicable internal, operational, security, regulatory and procurement requirements, participating TSOs may engage with selected bidders as potential users and contribute to the validation and demonstration of proposed solutions. The involvement of ENTSO-E and/or individual TSOs in the development of the thematic scope, use cases, consultations or other activities associated with this Call does not constitute an endorsement, certification, commitment to participate in a pilot, commitment to procure or purchase any solution, or any other contractual or commercial commitment. Any future participation, testing, procurement or deployment by an individual TSO will be subject to its own decision-making processes, applicable legal, regulatory, security, operational and procurement requirements. Topics of Relevance  The use cases are organised under two complementary challenge areas, reflecting the operational needs identified by ENTSO-E in relation to the secure and resilient operation of Europe's interconnected electricity transmission system.  The proposed activities build on existing space-enabled capabilities and services, including Earth observation, positioning, navigation and timing, and satellite communications. The objective is therefore not to develop these capabilities in isolation, but to demonstrate their operational value for TSOs and explore how they can complement existing terrestrial solutions, strengthen resilience and support continuity of grid operations.  The two themes will open for applications one after the other: Theme 1 applications are invited from November 4 2026 to January 29 2027, Theme 2 applications will be invited from February 1 2027 to 30 April 2027. Theme 1 | Situational Awareness for Critical Events  | Opening: 2.11.2026 | Closing: 29.01.2027 Developing solutions that improve the ability of Transmission System Operators to anticipate, detect, understand and assess risks affecting electricity transmission infrastructure and system stability through enhanced awareness of environmental hazards, infrastructure condition and evolving operational risks. Key capabilities:​   Early detection and monitoring of wildfires, floods, extreme weather, and infrastructure failures​  Monitoring of transmission corridors, vegetation encroachment, and environmental risks​  Integration of space weather information for grid risk forecasting​  Post-event damage assessment and operational recovery support​  Scalable and interoperable platforms supporting use across multiple transmission system environments, subject to applicable requirements Theme 2 | Strengthening Operational Resilience for the Grid | Opening: 1.2.2027 | Closing: 30.4.2027 Enhancing the resilience, security and continuity of grid operations through improved operational capabilities, communications, positioning, timing and emergency response services that support effective operation during normal and degraded conditions. Key capabilities:​   High-accuracy and resilient timing capabilities for applications within digital substations and other grid applications requiring stringent timing performance, subject to applicable technical and security requirements ​   Precise positioning for onshore and offshore grid assets​   Detection of interference, spoofing, and signal degradation​   Satellite backup communications when terrestrial networks fail​   Secure connectivity for grid restoration and emergency operations     Value of Space  Space assets provide critical capabilities to support grid resilience:​   Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO) data can provide valuable capabilities for monitoring infrastructure, environmental risks and to assess damage.   SatEO provides wide-area, persistent monitoring of transmission corridors and substations, enabling near real-time detection and forecasting of wildfires, and supporting rapid flood mapping and post-event damage assessment. SatEO also allows operators to monitor vegetation  encroachment and construction activities that may impact the grid and to detect ground deformation using radar techniques, identifying subsidence or structural movements that could affect critical infrastructure.     Satellite Navigation (SatNav) can provide high-precision positioning capabilities that may support applications within digital sub-stations and other grid assets requiring a stringent synchronisation performance. SatNav can also enable the detection of structural displacement or slow asset movement, and provides independent, resilient timing sources that migrate risks associated with terrestrial timing failures or signal interference.      Satellite Communications
